name: X-Plane 12 with the PX4 plugin
summary: X-Plane is a paid Windows flight simulator. A community plugin, px4xplane, connects it to PX4 running in WSL. Drone Deck cannot download or install either: install them yourself, then choose the X-Plane folder and check it.

guide.title: Install X-Plane 12
guide.body: Buy X-Plane 12 from Laminar Research and install it on Windows. It is a paid product, so Drone Deck cannot install it for you.

guide.title: Install the px4xplane plugin
guide.body: Download the px4xplane release for your PX4 version and unzip it into X-Plane's Resources/plugins folder, so that Resources/plugins/px4xplane exists.

guide.title: Configure the plugin
guide.body: Follow the plugin's instructions to pick the airframe and connect to PX4. PX4 runs in WSL, which Windows reaches at 127.0.0.1. Windows may ask about the firewall the first time; that choice is yours.

guide.title: Choose the folder and check
guide.body: Choose your X-Plane folder, then Check. Drone Deck looks for X-Plane.exe and the plugin folder. Whether PX4 and X-Plane actually talk is only known once the workspace starts.

privileges: Whatever the X-Plane installer asks for
verification: X-Plane.exe and Resources/plugins/px4xplane exist in the chosen folder

name: Webots
summary: Webots is an open-source robot simulator. ArduPilot SITL flies in Webots worlds that ship with ArduPilot's source. Install Webots yourself on Windows, then choose its program and check it.
steps: Open ArduPilot's Webots world when the workspace starts

guide.title: Install Webots
guide.body: Download the Windows installer from Cyberbotics and install it. Webots is free and open source; Drone Deck does not download it for you.

guide.title: Choose the Webots program and check
guide.body: Choose webotsw.exe in the Webots installation folder (under msys64\mingw64\bin), then Check.

guide.title: Open ArduPilot's world
guide.body: When the workspace starts, open a world from ArduPilot's libraries/SITL/examples/Webots_Python/worlds folder in Webots (File > Open World; the folder is inside WSL under \\wsl.localhost). ArduPilot SITL waits until the world runs.

guide.title: WSL networking
guide.body: ArduPilot in WSL and Webots on Windows exchange data over UDP. If SITL never connects, WSL's mirrored networking (networkingMode=mirrored in .wslconfig) lets both use 127.0.0.1. Windows may ask about the firewall; that choice is yours.

privileges: Whatever the Webots installer asks for
verification: The chosen program is a Windows executable

name: RealFlight with FlightAxis
summary: RealFlight is a paid Windows RC flight simulator. ArduPilot SITL drives a RealFlight model over its FlightAxis link. Install RealFlight yourself, enable FlightAxis, then choose its program and check it.

guide.title: Install RealFlight
guide.body: Buy RealFlight 8, 9 or Evolution and install it on Windows. It is a paid product, so Drone Deck cannot install it for you.

guide.title: Enable FlightAxis and load a model
guide.body: In RealFlight's settings, enable the FlightAxis link, then load a model prepared for ArduPilot. ArduPilot's guide lists the models and settings.

guide.title: Tell ArduPilot where RealFlight runs
guide.body: ArduPilot SITL runs in WSL and connects to RealFlight on Windows. Set the system's RealFlight computer to the address WSL reaches Windows at: 127.0.0.1 with WSL's mirrored networking, otherwise the Windows address WSL sees as its gateway. Windows may ask about the firewall; that choice is yours.

guide.title: Choose the RealFlight program and check
guide.body: Choose RealFlight's program file, then Check. Whether ArduPilot reaches FlightAxis is only known once the workspace starts.

privileges: Whatever the RealFlight installer asks for
verification: The chosen program is a Windows executable
